skill.name: agentic-structure
skill.description: Collaborative programming guidelines for safe, maintainable agent-assisted software development. It helps teams structure implementation, discussion, security, error handling, comments, and knowledge-sharing workflows.
skill.summary: Guide agent-assisted coding with clear process, security, and maintainability rules.
skill.author: BackGwa

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by benign guideline language and defensive security examples. The skill is a documentation-only programming framework with read-only allowed tools and no evidence of prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, command execution, or unsafe network behavior.

static_findings.snippet: - Avoid vague names (`data`, `temp`, `handle`, `util`) unless the scope is extremely small and obvio
- **Avoid over-fragmentation** - Don't split related code just for the sake of small files
### Avoid Over-Fragmentation
- Avoid scattering related code by type only (all models in one folder, all controllers in another)
- Avoid copy-paste duplication when the logic is meaningfully the same.
- Avoid swallowing errors; when you catch, either:
- Validate inputs early to prevent invalid states from propagating.
- Be mindful of resource safety (memory, file handles, network connections) and avoid leaks.
AFTER: First check if order is missing or invalid and return early. Then loop through each item, ski
Avoid abstraction when:
- **Prefer clarity in code over comments**: Use clear naming and simple control flow to avoid needin
- **Avoid comment noise**: Excessive comments reduce readability and make maintenance harder.
#### Signal Low - Generally avoid unless there's a clear reason to comment
Avoid comments that restate the code or appear on every line:
Avoid over-documentation; it can reduce readability and quickly become outdated.
- [ ] Multiple valid approaches exist with different trade-offs
- Create a step-by-step plan to solve the problem; avoid trying to finish everything at once.
- Avoid unnecessary abstraction; only introduce patterns that will be reused.
- Multiple valid interpretations exist.
- [ ] Existing tests still pass
- [ ] Request references "similar to X" but X has multiple valid interpretations
| "robust" | "What failure scenarios? (network issues, invalid input, high load, service outages)" |
- [ ] Multiple valid implementation approaches exist with different trade-offs
#### Signal Low - Generally avoid unless there's a compelling reason
#### Patterns to Avoid
- Validate inputs early so invalid states do not flow inward.
- Non-recoverable failures: invalid input, domain rule violations, authorization failures
- [ ] Multiple valid interpretations exist that code exploration doesn't resolve
- Ask SPECIFIC questions (avoid "please provide more details")
- Add repository hygiene: `.gitignore` local secret files; avoid committing `.env` files.
- Private keys, signing keys, encryption keys
- Do not use fast general-purpose hashes (e.g., MD5, SHA-1, raw SHA-256) for passwords.
- Add repository hygiene: `.gitignore` local secret files; avoid committing `.env` files.
- Prefer Argon2id (recommended), or bcrypt/scrypt when Argon2id is unavailable.
- User tier (free vs paid accounts)
- Avoid leaking whether an account exists in rate limit responses
- Avoid leaking sensitive data in logs, errors, or analytics.

content.value_statement: Agent-assisted coding can drift into unclear scope, weak validation, or inconsistent style. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured guidelines for safer collaboration and maintainable delivery.
actual_capabilities: Guides feature work through clarification, planning, implementation, validation, and feedback steps.
Provides coding standards for naming, file organization, reuse, control flow, and maintainability.
Defines security guidance for secrets, hashing, authentication, rate limiting, uploads, and production exposure.
Supplies rules for high-signal comments and avoiding noisy documentation.
Explains when to ask users for decisions and how to present trade-offs.
Includes protocols for handling knowledge gaps and requesting precise missing information.
limitations: It is a guideline set, not an automated scanner or code generator.
It does not include executable scripts, tests, or project-specific configuration.
Teams must adapt the advice to their stack, threat model, and delivery process.
It cannot verify that generated code follows the guidelines without separate review or testing.

use_cases.title: Structure a New Feature
use_cases.description: Use the development process to split work into core logic, integration, interface, and validation steps.

use_cases.title: Improve Agent Collaboration
use_cases.description: Use the discussion rules to clarify ambiguous requirements and present trade-offs before implementation.

use_cases.title: Apply Secure Defaults
use_cases.description: Use the security guidelines when handling secrets, authentication, uploads, rate limits, and production exposure.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Small Feature
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin a straightforward implementation with clear scope.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Agentic Structure to plan and implement this feature in small validated steps: [describe feature].

prompt_templates.title: Clarify an Ambiguous Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the discussion guidelines to identify ambiguities in this request and ask only the questions needed to proceed: [paste request].

prompt_templates.title: Review Code Quality Direction
prompt_templates.scenario: Check whether a planned change fits maintainability guidance.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the coding standards and error handling guidelines to review this implementation plan for clarity, safety, and unnecessary abstraction: [paste plan].

prompt_templates.title: Design a Secure Implementation Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a feature that touches sensitive data or public inputs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Agentic Structure to propose a secure implementation sequence for this feature, including validation checkpoints and user decisions: [describe feature and constraints].

output_examples.input: Plan a user profile update feature with validation and error handling.
output: A prioritized implementation order that starts with core validation logic.
A list of user decisions needed before changing public behavior.
Validation checkpoints for successful updates, invalid input, and authorization failures.

output_examples.input: This request says the API should be robust. What should we ask?
output: Targeted questions about failure scenarios, load, network behavior, and expected user-facing errors.
A recommended default if the user wants the agent to proceed.

output_examples.input: Review whether comments are needed for this tricky authentication helper.
output: A recommendation to improve names or structure first.
A short explanation of any non-obvious security assumption that deserves one comment.
A warning against comments that restate visible code behavior.

best_practices: Use the guideline selection matrix before asking an agent to implement a broad task.
Validate each completed step with tests or observable behavior before moving on.
Apply the security guidelines first when requirements involve secrets, user input, authentication, or uploads.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the skill as a replacement for project-specific security review.
Do not force every guideline when a smaller focused reference is enough.
Do not skip user approval when the change affects architecture, dependencies, schema, or security posture.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It provides structured programming guidelines for agent-assisted software work, including planning, coding standards, security, comments, errors, and knowledge gaps.

faq.question: Does it execute code or change files by itself?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation-based and declares only read-oriented tools in its metadata.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when starting implementation work, clarifying requirements, handling security-sensitive code, writing comments, or managing missing information.

faq.question: Can it replace team coding standards?
faq.answer: No. It can complement team standards, but project-specific rules and security requirements should take priority.

faq.question: Why were security patterns flagged in the audit?
faq.answer: The static scanner matched words related to secrets, hashes, and system safety. Manual review found these were defensive examples, not harmful instructions.
